questions.question:
Hot water can be a pollutant if it comes from:

(a) A hot spring (b) A power plant (c) An industry
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Both (b) and (c)**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Thermal pollution** is the degradation of water quality by any process that **changes the ambient water temperature.**
 
• **Hot water can be a pollutant if it comes from A power plant, An industry.**
 
• Heat is classified as a** water pollutant** when it is caused by heated industrial effluents or from **anthropogenic** (human) alterations of stream bank vegetation that increase the water system temperatures.
 
• A common cause of **thermal pollution** is the** **use of water as a **coolant by power plants **and** industrial manufacturers.**
 
• When the water used as a coolant is returned to the natural environment at a higher temperature, the** **sudden change in** temperature decreases the oxygen supply** and** affects the ecosystem.**
 
• Fish and other organisms adapted to a particular temperature range can be killed by an abrupt change in **water temperature** (either a rapid increase or decrease in the temperature of the water known as** thermal shock**).

questions.question: In order to get clean drinking water disinfectant is used after filtration. Disinfectant, however, is NOT used for removing:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**minerals.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The goal of disinfection of public water supplies is:**

 
 
• **elimination of the pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, and parasites that are responsible for waterborne diseases.**
 
 
 
• **Chlorine and chloramine are the major disinfectants** used in public water systems.
 
• Chlorine** kills pathogens** such as bacteria and viruses** by breaking the chemical bonds in their molecules.**
 
• **Boiling water is the most effective way to disinfect water.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Need for disinfection of drinking water.**

 
 
• **Water from lakes, rivers, streams and many groundwater sources may contain disease-causing “germs.”**
 
• The germs, called** pathogens, can lead to water-borne infections.**
 
• **Water-borne illnesses **can lead to **serious complications,** including death.
 
• Water-borne** infections can spread** when an animal or human feces containing these **pathogens get into drinking water.**
 
• These pathogens may include bacteria, viruses, or parasites (e.g.,** Campylobacter, Salmonella, Giardia, and Cryptosporidium**).
 
• **Disinfection kills or removes pathogens **from drinking water, reducing health risks.
 
• One can disinfect water by **adding chemicals, using heat, using ultraviolet (UV) radiation, and filtration.**

questions.question: Solids like fats, grease and oil that float on top of liquid wastewater is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** sludge.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Floatable materials like fats, grease, and oil that float on top of liquid wastewater are called sludge.**
 
• The** process of skimming is used to remove these materials** and make water fit for use.
 
• **Skimming tank:**
 
 
• A** chamber** used for sludge removal where matter** like oil, fat, grease, etc. floats on the surface.**
 
• They then remain on the surface of the wastewater (Sewage) until removed.
 
• While the liquid flows out continuously under partitions or baffles.​
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Sewage treatment:**

 
 
• **Process of removing contaminants from municipal wastewater.**
 
• Wastewater contains mainly **household sewage plus some industrial wastewater. **
 
• Sewage treatment units are** normally designed for 15-20 years.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Compost**

 
 
• ​Compost is** decomposed organic material.**
 
• **Made with materials such as leaves, shredded twigs, and kitchen scraps from plants.**
 
• It is a **great material for garden soil.**
 
 
 
• **Peat​**
 
 
• ​Peat is the** surface organic layer of soil.**
 
• It consists of **partially decomposed organic matter,** derived mostly from plant material.
 
• It **forms due to accumulation under conditions of waterlogging, oxygen deficiency, high acidity, and nutrient deficiency.**
 
 
 
• **Urea​**
 
 
• **​Urea is a source of Nitrogen**, an essential** nutrient crucial for crop growth and development.**
 
• Urea is the most** important nitrogenous fertilizer in the country.**
 
• It also has **industrial applications such as the production of plastics and as a nutritional supplement for cattle.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT known as a Greenhouse Gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Greenhouse gases **are known so as they act like a greenhouse on the surface of the planet.
 
• Greenhouse gases are known as heat-trapping gases as they increase the temperature of the atmosphere by trapping heat.
 
• The greenhouse effect leads to the cause of global warming.
 
• The primary greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere are:
 
 
• water vapour (H2O),
 
• carbon dioxide (CO2),
 
• methane (CH4),
 
• nitrous oxide (N2O), and
 
• ozone (O3).
 
 
 
• Methane, Nitrous oxide, and Carbon dioxide are the primary greenhouse gases related to agriculture.

**Hence Oxygen is NOT known as a greenhouse gas.**

questions.question: The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) declared Koraput Traditional Agriculture as a 'Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System' (GIAHS) in the year ______.
questions.solution:

__
 
• Koraput Traditional Agriculture is India's Traditional system in the **Koraput Region of Odisha** which is strongly linked to the local traditional communities.
 
• Through this system, high biodiversity has been conserved through** in-situ conservation preserving endemic species**.
 
• The system has helped conserve the **rich floristic diversity consisting of about 2500 species of flowering plants**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• ​It helps identify ways to mitigate threats faced by these systems and their people and enhance the benefits derived from these dynamic systems.
 
• There are three recognised GIAHS sites in India - **Kuttanad Below Sea Level Farming System of Kerala, Koraput Traditional Agriculture of Odisha and Pampore Saffron Heritage of Kashmir**.

questions.question: _______ are the producers and consumers of the earth’s resources.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human beings.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Human beings** are the producers and consumers of the earth’s resources.
 
• Human beings are the producers and consumers because they only produce food in the earth.
 
• And they also depend on plants and animals to eat.so humans are called the **producers and consumers.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Every organism depends on other organisms for food material and all organisms are (producers to consumers) arranged in series in which food energy is transferred through repeated eating and being eaten.
 
• The green plant in the ecosystem is called producers.
 
• Producers prepare food from solar energy(sun).
 
• All the heterotrophs of the ecosystem are known as consumers.
 
• Consumer, directly and indirectly, depends on the producers for food.

questions.question: Acid rain is caused by the chemical reaction that begins when compounds like sulphur dioxides and ______ are released into the air.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nitrogen oxides.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Acid rain is caused by the chemical reaction that begins when compounds like **sulphur dioxides and ****nitrogen oxides** are released into the air.

 
• Normal rain has a pH of about 5.6; it is slightly acidic because carbon dioxide (CO₂) dissolves into it forming weak carbonic acid. 
 
• Acid rain usually has a pH between 4.2 and 4.4.
 
• Acid rain, or acid deposition, is a broad term that includes any form of precipitation with acidic components.
 
• Such as sulfuric or nitric acid that fall to the ground from the atmosphere in wet or dry forms. 
 
• This can include rain, snow, fog, hail or even dust that is acidic.
 
• Acid rain results when sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOX) are emitted into the atmosphere and transported by wind and air currents.
 
• The SO₂ and NOX react with water, oxygen, and other chemicals to form sulfuric and nitric acids. 
 
• These then mix with water and other materials before falling to the ground.

questions.question: How many pollutants are included to measure Air Quality Index in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The National Air Quality Index (AQI)** reduces complex data on **eight pollutants to a single number (index value), **nomenclature, and colour.
 
• On October 17, 2014, the National Air Quality Index (AQI) was launched to provide information on air quality to the general public in an easily understandable format.
 
• Air quality is measured using eight pollutants:
 
 
• **Particulate Matter (size less than 10 µm) or (PM10), **
 
• **Particulate Matter (size less than 2.5 µm) or (PM2.5),**
 
• **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂),**
 
• **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂),**
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO),**
 
• **Ozone (O₃),**
 
• **Ammonia (NH₃), and**
 
• **Lead (Pb)**
 
 
 
• It should be noted that in India, ambient air quality criteria are set independently for around 12 pollutants, including the eight that make up the Air Quality Index.
 
• Air quality is divided into six categories by the AQI. **Good, Satisfactory, Moderately polluted, Poor, Very Poor, and Severe **are the categories.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an abiotic component of the eco system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Living Organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ecosystem**- The word Ecosystem was termed by 'Arthur Tansley' which means an interaction that occurs between Biotic and Abiotic components.
 
• The ecosystem is divided into two components Biotic and Abiotic components.
 
• **Abiotic components** consist of **Sunlight, oxygen, moisture, minerals, temperature, soil and water**.
 
• **Biotic components **consist of **Living organisms which are Plants (Producers) and Animals (Consumers)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/377faffe87f801fad37875fa8fe3fd5faa70648e1d3407f7e9052989a44ae655.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c829f5ca45562d2fd6ae56d8048d2693ba38c47b6c136e3a68efc5475407cb0d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Producers**
 **Consumers**
 
 

 They are also called autotrophs.
 They are also known as Heterotropes
 
 

 An autotroph is an organism that can produce its own food in presence of sunlight or with the help of chemicals.
 Heterotrophs are animals which feed on other living organisms.
 
 

 They can perform photosynthesis and chemosynthesis to prepare food.
 They are further divided into Herbivores, carnivores and Omnivores.
 
 

 
 
Photosynthesis is done in the presence of sunlight by terrestrial and water plants (depth of 200 m).

 
Chemosynthesis is done in absence of sunlight by plants living in deep oceans.

 
 
 
Herbivores are animals which feed on plants.

 
Carnivores are animals which feed on other animals.

 
Omnivores are animals which eat both plants and animals.

questions.question: What are the two variables whose relationship is given by the environmental Kuznets curve?

options.text: Environmental degradation and per capita income

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Environmental degradation and per capita income.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Environmental Kuznets curve:**

 
 
• **The environmental Kuznets curve (EKC) is a relationship between environmental quality and economic development.**
 
• According to this theory, **many indicators of environmental degradation tend to get worse as modern economic growth occurs until average income reaches a certain point over the course of development.**
 
• In other words, the **environmental Kuznets curve suggests that economic development initially leads to a deterioration in the environment,** but after a **certain level of economic growth, a society begins to improve its relationship with the environment, and levels of environmental degradation reduce.**
 
• The EKC suggests that the **solution to pollution is economic growth**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This is a **debatable theory**.
 
• The link **between levels of income and environmental degradation is quite weak.**
 
• It is possible economic growth will be compatible with an improved environment, but it requires a very deliberate set of policies and willingness to produce energy and goods in the most environmentally friendly way.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac37500ee6ca3343237732bfa68af8ca1d9e9735deef226a9afbaad3dd404f2e.png]

questions.question: An ecosystem consists of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biotic and abiotic components.**__

__
 
• An ecosystem consists of **Biotic and abiotic components.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• An ecosystem consists of a community of organisms together with their physical environment consists of two components Biotic and Abiotic.
 
 
• ** Biotic **consists of living organisms **(Producers, Consumers, Decomposers).**
 
• **Abiotic** consists of non-living organisms **(air, water, soil, and Sunlight).**
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The food chain is a linear sequence of organisms where nutrients and energy transferred from one organism to another.
 
 
• ** Producers**__ make their own food. Producers** **include all autotrophs such as plants. They are called **autotrophs** as they can produce food through the process of **photosynthesis.**
 
• __**Primary Consumers**__ depend on the producers. Example - Rat.
 
• __**Secondary consumers**__ depend on the primary consumer for energy. Example- Snake
 
• __**Tertiary consumers**__ depend on the secondary consumers for the food. Example- Eagle
 
• __**Decomposers **__are microorganisms that decompose the dead and decaying material into humus which enriches the soil. Example - Bacteria, Fungus.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• Father of Ecosystem - **Arthur Tansley**
